explain: Reads bytes from disk through the kernel's VFS layer (open/read syscalls). The page cache usually serves repeated reads from RAM.
Writes go to the page cache first; data reaches the device later unless fsync is called.
Subscribes to kernel file-change notifications (inotify on Linux, FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows).
Starts another program. The OS forks/execs (CreateProcess on Windows) a new process with its own address space.
Creates an OS thread that shares memory with its parent. The scheduler time-slices threads across CPU cores.
Schedules a cooperative task on an event loop or async runtime. It yields at await points instead of blocking a thread.
Asks the runtime to wake code after a delay. Timers are backed by the event loop or a kernel timer facility.
Reads configuration from the process environment block, inherited from the parent process at start.
Reacts to asynchronous OS notifications such as SIGINT/SIGTERM (Ctrl+C, shutdown).
Allocates a contiguous block of memory. Large buffers may be backed by mmap'd pages.
Serialises access to shared memory so only one thread enters a critical section. Contention parks threads in the kernel (futex).
Passes messages between threads or tasks instead of sharing memory.
Pulls entropy from the OS CSPRNG (getrandom, /dev/urandom, BCryptGenRandom).
Computes a fixed-size digest (SHA-256, blake3), used for integrity checks, cache keys and signatures.
Trades CPU for fewer bytes (gzip/deflate, brotli, zstd). Decompression is usually much faster than compression.
Writes diagnostic lines to stdout/stderr or a file. Synchronous logging on hot paths can become a bottleneck.
Reads the terminal/pipe input or writes to stdout; the OS buffers file descriptors 0/1/2.
Offloads parallel math to the GPU via a driver API (CUDA, Metal, WebGPU).
Opens (or reuses) a TCP connection, optionally wraps it in TLS, sends an HTTP request and waits for the response.
Binds a listening TCP socket, accepts connections and parses incoming HTTP requests into handler calls.
Maps an HTTP method + path pattern to a handler function in the server's router table.
Code that runs before/after every request (auth, CORS, logging). Requests pass through the chain before reaching a route.
Upgrades an HTTP connection into a long-lived, full-duplex message channel.
A byte stream between two endpoints with ordered, reliable delivery (handshake, acks, retransmits).
Resolves a hostname to IP addresses via the system resolver (stub resolver, then a recursive DNS server).
A typed RPC over HTTP/2 using Protocol Buffers for the payload.
Signs or verifies a JSON Web Token (base64 header.payload plus a signature), checked on every request.
Derives a slow, salted hash (bcrypt/argon2/scrypt) so stolen hashes are expensive to crack.
The browser blocks cross-origin requests unless the server returns Access-Control-Allow-* headers.
Caps requests per client per time window, usually with a token bucket held in memory or Redis.
A one-way stream of text events over a single long-lived HTTP response.
Forwards incoming requests to another server (API gateway, dev proxy), often rewriting paths or adding auth headers.
Splits a URL into scheme, host, path and query so routing and requests use the right parts.
Sends SQL text to the database, which parses it, plans it (index or scan) and returns rows.
An ORM turns a method call into a SELECT. Watch for N+1 queries when loading relations in a loop.
An ORM turns object changes into INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, usually inside a transaction flushed on commit.
Groups statements so they commit or roll back together (ACID). The isolation level decides what concurrent transactions see.
Versioned DDL changes (CREATE/ALTER TABLE) applied in order so every environment has the same schema.
An in-memory key-value store reached over TCP. Reads take well under a millisecond; keys can expire with TTLs.
Stores results of pure calls in process memory so repeated inputs skip recomputation.
Stores JSON-like documents (MongoDB, Firestore). Queries match fields; joins happen in the application.
An inverted index maps words to documents so text queries avoid scanning every row.
Converts objects to JSON text and back. Cost grows with payload size; huge payloads block the event loop.
Checks untrusted input against a schema before it reaches business logic or the database.
UI state held in the browser. Changing it re-renders the components that read it.
Client-side cache of server data (React Query, SWR) with background refetch and request de-duplication.
Data persisted in the browser (localStorage, IndexedDB, cookies). It survives reloads and is scoped per origin.
Receives a multipart/form-data body and streams the file to disk or object storage.
Returns large result sets in pages (LIMIT/OFFSET or cursors) to bound memory and latency.
Stores blobs by key in a bucket over HTTPS. Cheap and durable, but every call is a network round trip.
Decouples producers and consumers. Messages wait durably until a worker acknowledges them (at-least-once delivery).
Work moved off the request path into a separate worker process that pulls jobs from a queue.
Publishes events to a topic and every subscriber gets a copy; used for fan-out between services.
Credentials loaded from a secret manager or the environment at runtime instead of being committed to source.
Hands a message to an SMTP server or provider API that queues and delivers it.
Calls a payment provider over HTTPS; money movement is confirmed asynchronously via webhooks.
Sends a prompt to a hosted language model over HTTPS and streams back generated tokens.
Ships logs, metrics or traces to a collector (OpenTelemetry, Sentry) for dashboards and alerts.
Talks to Docker/Kubernetes APIs to start isolated processes with their own filesystem and network namespace.
Code that runs per event on managed infrastructure; instances start on demand (cold starts) and scale automatically.
